page: Amazon Web Services g7e.8xlarge is a GPU-accelerated cloud server instance optimized for graphics-intensive and compute-dense processing on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features 32 vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8559C processor running at 2.4 GHz, backed by 320 MB of L3 cache. System memory comprises 256 GB of DDR5 RAM operating at 6 GHz, establishing an 8 GB per core ratio. Hardware accelerators include a single NVIDIA Blackwell RTX PRO 6000 GPU with 96 GB of dedicated VRAM. The system is bundled with 1900 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and maintains a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate top-tier performance for artificial intelligence workloads, specifically in large language model (LLM) prompt processing and text generation across small, medium, and large models. Single-core Geekbench processing, image processing, and gzip compression exhibit top-tier to strong performance metrics. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reaches 198.11 GB/sec, while static web serving throughput measures 59.95 GB/sec. Multi-core execution in stress-ng CPU tests, PassMark database operations, and Redis set operations align with average benchmark tiers.

The configuration provides qualitative resource density by combining a high-capacity 96 GB VRAM Blackwell GPU with 256 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory and direct NVMe local storage. While standard multi-core CPU workloads execute at average levels, hardware acceleration via Intel AMX matrix extensions and the NVIDIA GPU offsets general compute constraints for tensor operations. The server is suited for LLM inference, computer vision processing, high-fidelity 3D graphics rendering, and memory-bound data science pipelines.
